sources.title: ASTM F3269-21 Standard Practice for Methods to Safely Bound Behavior of Aircraft Systems Containing Complex Functions Using Run-Time Assurance (public product page)
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public ASTM product page; inspected its status line, scope (1.1) and significance-and-use (4.1) text. The standard itself was not accessed.

regions.locator: Product page: status, scope 1.1 and significance and use 4.1
regions.excerpt: This practice provides an architectural framework for developing an RTA system, which provides run-time assurance as an alternative to design-time assurance to fulfill safety requirements for an unassured or complex function.

sources.limitations: Public abstract of a paywalled consensus standard practice. It does not show regulator acceptance for a particular product, and says nothing about whether a monitor can observe a given perception failure.

sources.title: AC 20-152A — Development Assurance for Airborne Electronic Hardware
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public FAA AC and inspected its purpose and recognized documents.

regions.excerpt: This AC recognizes EUROCAE ED-80, Design Assurance Guidance for Airborne Electronic Hardware, dated April 2000, and RTCA DO-254

sources.limitations: Acceptable, non-exclusive means for electronic hardware; not the licensed DO-254 text and not ML-specific guidance.

sources.title: AC 20-193 — Use of Multi-Core Processors
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public FAA AC and inspected its purpose, exceptions (2.7) and background on interference (3.1-3.4).

regions.excerpt: Interference between the software applications or tasks executing on an MCP could cause safety-critical software applications to behave in a non-deterministic or unsafe manner

sources.limitations: Multi-core processor guidance; not an ML inference or GPU certification method, and its exceptions depend on how cores are configured.

sources.title: NASA-STD-7009B — Standard for Models and Simulations
sources.publisher: NASA Office of the Chief Engineer
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public 88-page PDF and inspected the approval date, foreword and purpose (1.1).

regions.excerpt: The primary purpose of this Standard is to reduce the risks associated with M&S-influenced decisions

sources.limitations: A NASA standard for models and simulations; not an automotive or aviation certification requirement, and it states what must be done, not how.

sources.title: STPA Handbook (MIT-STAMP-001)
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public handbook and inspected chapter 1's definition of STPA and its causation model.

regions.excerpt: In addition to component failures, STPA assumes that accidents can also be caused by unsafe interactions of system components, none of which may have failed.

sources.limitations: A method handbook; it does not by itself establish regulatory acceptance. Road practice references STPA through SAE J3187, which was not accessed.

sources.title: UN Regulation No 157 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regards to Automated Lane Keeping Systems [2021/389] (catalog record)
sources.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union
sources.jurisdiction: EU publication of a UNECE regulation
sources.inspection_scope: Retained the public catalog page; inspected its title only. The regulation text was not retrieved (EUR-Lex blocked automated access).

regions.excerpt: UN Regulation No 157 – Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regards to Automated Lane Keeping Systems [2021/389]

sources.limitations: Bibliographic record only; establishes that the EU publishes R157 as an approval regulation, not its content or application details.
